capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia lists the 3rd-generation pack as 17.6 kWh without a gross/usable label; the 2017 car of the same capacity is given as 17.6 total.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: basis: the German Wikipedia ED4 (2017-24) row, 16.7 kWh usable of the same 17.6 kWh capacity, applied to the ED3 pack (ev-database and iSeeCars list 16.7 for 2013-15, per the fact-checker; not opened). English Wikipedia gives 17.2 usable for the 2017 car, so the figure may be 16.7-17.2.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: GUESS: Wikipedia says lithium-ion by Deutsche Accumotive (the 2017 car "LG chemistry, 96 cells"); LG Chem cells are NMC but no page says so. Owner decision.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: GUESS: no page states the pack voltage; the 2017 pack has 96 cells in series (Wikipedia), about 350 V nominal, and the ED2/ED3 packs are assumed the same class. Owner decision.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare: no DC fast charging, and no battery-warming feature is described for the smart ED on any page opened.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia states 3.3 kW for the ED2 car; the EPA 240 V charge time (6 h for the 2013 car, vs 3 h in 2017 with 7.2 kW) is consistent with the same charger on the ED3. German Wikipedia says 3.7 kW for the EU ED3 and Fleetnews (per the fact-checker) 3 kW; no North American page for 2013-16.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare (ED2 page): "does not support DC fast charging"; other years assumed the same (EPA lists only 240 V charge times; the 2012 optional quick-charge announcement was for Europe).
